_doc.purpose: Language-agnostic single source of truth describing malicious/corrupt .qzdb test inputs. Extracted and deduplicated from existing per-language fail-closed / hostile test suites. Consumed by fail-closed suites across all 8 SDKs (Java first). Each consumer resolves byte offsets from its OWN parsed header at runtime; absolute offsets are intentionally NOT baked in because the .qzdb layout varies per file (v4/v6 presence, node24 flag, pool count, geo count all shift section offsets).
_doc.how_to_consume: 1) Load a real .qzdb into bytes. 2) Parse the 192-byte header to resolve the anchors in `anchor_table`. 3) Apply the `mutation` recipe to the bytes. 4) Feed the mutated bytes to the SDK's open-from-bytes path. 5) Assert `expected_outcome` holds (fail_closed + one of error_code_any, or GracefulNull). Do NOT modify production SDK code or existing test files; this file is the shared fixture.
_doc.mutation_schema: Each `mutation` is an object with a `type` (one of the op types below) plus type-specific fields. A `compound` mutation applies an ordered list of `steps` (each a mutation object) to the same bytes.

op_types.header_field: Overwrite a fixed header field. fields: offset(int 0..192), width(1|2|4|8|48), value(int), endian('le'), mask(optional int, XORed with current value instead of overwrite). width=48 writes a 48-bit little-endian value across 6 bytes.
op_types.header_byte_sweep: For offset in [start,end): write each pattern in `patterns` (array of ints 0..255), one mutated copy per pattern. fields: start, end, patterns.
op_types.header_field_sweep: For each offset in `offsets` (array of ints): write `value` (width `width`, endian `endian`). fields: offsets, width, value, endian.
op_types.truncate: Truncate file. fields: bytes(int, absolute length) OR mode('to_zero'|'below_header'|'at_header'|'sweep'). 'below_header' = truncate to 100 bytes (< 192). 'at_header' = truncate to 191 bytes. 'sweep' = geometric lengths [0,1,2,4,8,...,file_size] (one mutated copy per length).
op_types.append_junk: Append bytes after EOF. fields: length(int), fill('random'|'zeros'|'0xFF').
op_types.section_mutate: Flip the first `span` bytes of a section. fields: anchor(str from anchor_table), span(int), patterns(array of ints 0..255) — one mutated copy per pattern.
op_types.trie_nodes_fill: Fill every trie node's pointer slots with a sentinel value (self-loop / forward-pointer attack). fields: anchor('trie_v4_nodes_start'|'trie_v6_nodes_start'), count_field('v4_node_count'|'v6_node_count'), value(int, e.g. 0x7FFFFFFF), write_width(4), sentinel(bool). Node stride is resolved by the consumer from header flags: bit4 (0x10) v4Node24 -> 6 bytes else 8; bit5 (0x20) v6Node24 -> 6 bytes else 8. For each node at anchor + i*stride, write `value` into the left pointer (offset 0) and right pointer (offset write_width) slots.
op_types.random_bitflips: Deterministic LCG bit flips over the first `span` bytes (or whole file if span='file'). fields: seed(int), rounds(int), max_flips(int), span(int|'file').
op_types.crc_field_corrupt: Flip the stored CRC field (header offset 16, 4 bytes LE) to a value that does NOT match the recomputed CRC (e.g. recomputed_crc XOR 0xFFFFFFFF). fields: none.

anchor_table.flags_field: header offset 8 (u16 LE); bit0 hasV4, bit1 hasV6, bit2 hasMetadata, bit4 v4Node24, bit5 v6Node24
anchor_table.v6jump_bits_field: header offset 11 (u8) — number of v6 jump-table bits

error_code_vocabulary.note: Canonical cross-language families. Map each SDK's native enum to these: C QZDB_ERR_* (-1..-8), Rust BadMagic/BadHeader/Unsupported/Corrupted/InvalidParam/OutOfBounds/NotFound/InvalidIp, Go BAD_MAGIC/BAD_HEADER/UNSUPPORTED/CORRUPTED/INVALID_PARAM, C# BadMagic/BadHeader/Unsupported/Corrupted/InvalidParam/InvalidIp, Python BAD_MAGIC/UNSUPPORTED/CORRUPTED/BAD_HEADER/INVALID_PARAM/OUT_OF_BOUNDS/NOT_FOUND, PHP ERROR_BAD_MAGIC(6)/ERROR_BAD_HEADER(5)/ERROR_UNSUPPORTED(7)/ERROR_CORRUPTED(2)/ERROR_INVALID_PARAM(4)/ERROR_NOT_FOUND(1).
error_code_vocabulary.GracefulNull: Extension code: the SDK returns empty/null/None WITHOUT throwing and WITHOUT returning wrong data. Used for attacks that degrade gracefully (e.g. C# hostile trie -> Find()==null). fail_closed is still true.

expected_outcome_semantics.fail_closed: bool. true = SDK must NOT crash, must NOT return plausibly-correct-but-wrong data, and must surface an error OR a graceful empty result.
expected_outcome_semantics.error_code_any: array of acceptable codes. If the SDK raises a structured error, its code must be in this list. If 'GracefulNull' is listed, a non-throwing empty/null result is also acceptable.

source_suites_legend.java: PROPOSED — not yet implemented (this file is the seed for it)

cases.description: Overwrite the 4-byte magic 'QZDB' at header offset 0 with wrong bytes (e.g. 'XXXX'). Every SDK must reject on open.

expected_outcome.notes: Universal. All 6 implemented suites assert BadMagic. Java: proposed.

cases.description: Set HeaderVersion (offset 4, u8) to an unsupported value (99).

expected_outcome.notes: Universal across C/Rust/Go/C#/Python/PHP. Java: proposed.

cases.description: Set VersionMask (offset 6, u16 LE) to an unsupported value (0xFFFF) so no known schema matches.

expected_outcome.notes: C/Rust/Go/C#/Python/PHP all reject unknown mask. Java: proposed.

cases.description: Flip the stored CRC field (offset 16, u32 LE) to a value that does not match the recomputed CRC.

expected_outcome.notes: Consistent: Rust Corrupted, Go CORRUPTED, C# Corrupted, Python CORRUPTED, C Corrupted. Java: proposed.

cases.description: Truncate the file to 0 bytes.

expected_outcome.notes: DIVERGENCE: C->Corrupted; Rust->BadMagic/BadHeader/Corrupted/InvalidParam (any); Go->CORRUPTED; C#->Corrupted (or BadMagic if <4 bytes); Python->CORRUPTED. error_code_any captures all.

cases.description: Truncate the file to 100 bytes (below the 192-byte header).

expected_outcome.notes: Same divergence family as truncate_to_zero. Java: proposed.

cases.description: Truncate the file to 191 bytes (just below the 192-byte header boundary).

expected_outcome.notes: Covered by C (truncate to 191) and Rust (header_bit_patterns includes 191). Java: proposed.

cases.description: Geometric sweep of truncation lengths [0,1,2,4,8,...,file_size]; each length is a separate mutated copy.

expected_outcome.notes: Rust-only sweep (truncate_sweep). Java: proposed.

cases.description: Set OffsetGeoEntries (header offset 104, u64 LE) to 1, pointing the geo section into the middle of the header.

expected_outcome.notes: C# malformed-offset test (OffsetGeoEntries=1). Rust/C also reject out-of-bounds section offsets. Java: proposed.

cases.description: Sweep every section-offset header field {40,48,64,72,80,88,96,104,136,144} to 1 (u64 LE). One mutated copy per offset.

expected_outcome.notes: C# badOffsetRejected sweeps these offsets. Java: proposed.

cases.description: Set a section offset (e.g. OffsetPools at 136) to a value far beyond the file size.

expected_outcome.notes: Rust out-of-bounds section offset; C rejects with Corrupted/OutOfBounds. Java: proposed.

cases.description: Fill every v4 trie node's left/right pointer slots with 0x7FFFFFFF (self-loop / forward-pointer), forcing infinite traversal or out-of-range node fetch.

expected_outcome.notes: DIVERGENCE: C# expects Find()==null (graceful, no throw) — represented as GracefulNull. Rust asserts no panic (Err or graceful). Java: proposed.

cases.description: Fill every v6 trie node's left/right pointer slots with 0x7FFFFFFF.

expected_outcome.notes: C# hostile v6 trie -> Find()==null. Java: proposed.

cases.description: Generic trie self-loop: corrupt a trie node so traversal loops or jumps out of bounds. Modeled as filling v4 nodes with a sentinel; consumers may additionally corrupt individual node pointers.

expected_outcome.notes: Rust/C assert no crash / no wrong data on hostile trie. Java: proposed.

cases.description: Set a pool offset field (OffsetPools at 136, u64) to 0x7FFFFFFF, far beyond the file.

expected_outcome.notes: Rust pool offset overflow; C rejects with OutOfBounds/Corrupted. Java: proposed.

cases.description: Set RowCount (offset 20, u32) to 0xFFFFFFFF.

expected_outcome.notes: Rust absurd row count; C rejects. Java: proposed.

cases.description: Set V4NodeCount (offset 152, u32) to 0xFFFFFFFF.

expected_outcome.notes: Rust absurd node count; C rejects. Java: proposed.

cases.description: Set V6NodeCount (offset 156, u32) to 0xFFFFFFFF.

expected_outcome.notes: Rust absurd node count; C rejects. Java: proposed.

cases.description: Set GeoCount (offset 14, u16) to 0xFFFF.

expected_outcome.notes: Rust absurd counts; C rejects. Java: proposed.

cases.description: Set IPRowSize (offset 160, u32) to 0 (or a huge value), breaking IPRow stride math.

expected_outcome.notes: Rust/C reject absurd IPRowSize. Java: proposed.

cases.description: Set GeoEntryGroupCount (offset 164, u32) to 0.

expected_outcome.notes: Rust zero group count; C rejects. Java: proposed.

cases.description: Craft a row whose group index exceeds GeoEntryGroupCount, so resolving the group reads out of bounds.

expected_outcome.notes: Rust invalid group index; C rejects. The compound is a representative recipe; consumers may craft a concrete row. Java: proposed.

cases.description: Append junk bytes after EOF (trailing garbage the parser must ignore or reject).

expected_outcome.notes: Rust append junk; C rejects trailing garbage. Some SDKs may ignore trailing bytes (GracefulNull) — both are fail-closed. Java: proposed.

cases.description: Sweep header bytes [4,192) writing each pattern in {0x00,0xFF,0x80,0x7F}; one mutated copy per (offset,pattern).

expected_outcome.notes: Rust header_bit_patterns. Java: proposed.

cases.description: Flip the first 64 bytes of each major section with patterns {0x00,0xFF,0x80,0x7F}; one mutated copy per (section,pattern).

expected_outcome.notes: Rust section_internal_mutation (applied to each section anchor). Java: proposed.

cases.description: Deterministic LCG random bit flips over the first 512KiB (or whole file).

expected_outcome.notes: Rust random_bitflips (deterministic seed). Java: proposed.

cases.description: Coordinated attack: set GeoEntryOffsets[0] (header offset 168, u48) to max, set group count, and craft a row so the resolver reads far out of bounds / wrong data.

expected_outcome.notes: Rust crafted_entry_offset_overflow (precise adversarial case). Java: proposed.

cases.description: PHP 'invalid' kind: a truncated / malformed database must surface an error rather than crash.

expected_outcome.notes: PHP tier2 'invalid' kind. Overlaps with truncate_below_header; kept distinct because PHP's harness drives it via golden_vectors 'invalid' entries. Java: proposed.

cases.description: PHP 'invalid' kind: a database with a bad section offset must surface an error.

expected_outcome.notes: PHP tier2 'invalid' kind (bad offset). Java: proposed.
